blocks.h2: Getting an Evanston Home Ready for Winter
blocks.body: Shut off outdoor faucets from the inside valve and drain them. Disconnect hoses. Insulate pipes in crawl spaces, unheated porches and outside walls you can reach. Seal drafts near pipes, especially on the windy side of the house. On the coldest nights, open cabinet doors under sinks on outside walls and let a faucet drip. If you'll be away, keep the heat on and ask a neighbor to check in.

blocks.h2: Burst Pipe Questions From Evanston Homeowners

items.q: How do I keep pipes from freezing?
items.preview: Heat, open cabinets and a slow drip.
items.answer: Keep the heat up, open cabinets on outside walls and let a faucet drip on the coldest nights.

items.q: Can I thaw a frozen pipe myself?
items.answer: Gently with a hair dryer or warm towels. Never use an open flame. If you can't reach it, call us.

items.q: Can you repair a pipe inside a plaster wall?
items.answer: Yes. We locate the break and open only what's needed.

items.q: Do I need to call if a pipe froze but didn't burst?
items.preview: Call if you can't thaw it safely.
items.answer: If you can't reach it or thaw it gently, call. A frozen pipe can split as it thaws.

items.q: Why did a pipe burst in a room that stays warm?
items.preview: The frozen spot may be elsewhere.
items.answer: The pipe can freeze in a cold wall or crawl space and split where pressure builds, sometimes in a warm room nearby.

items.q: How much does burst pipe repair cost in Evanston?
items.preview: It depends on the break. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the pipe burst and how we reach it. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
